market.what: firefighting foam concentrate (Class B AFFF + F3), world
market.method: report $869M (2024); bottom-up ~110M L/yr x ~$7/L (bulk $25-45/gal) = ~$0.8B; other reports at $5.9B look inflated

value.logic: NFPA 11 rate 0.16 gpm/ft2 for F3 vs 0.10 for AFFF: a surfactant giving AFFF-level film/fuel resistance cuts foam ~37% on ~$0.85B = ~$0.3B/yr, plus smaller tanks/pumps (not counted)
value.revenue_logic: surfactant ~20% of concentrate cost = ~$170M; ~7% share sold to foam makers = ~$12M
value.margin_logic: specialty surfactant (siloxane/glycoside class), 1-2 step from commodity inputs

trend.drivers: forced AFFF replacement: EU Reg 2025/1988, US DoD/state bans, airports (FAA allows F3 since 2023)
trend.deadline: EU: portable extinguishers 23 Oct 2026; all uses except Seveso by 23 Oct 2030

competition.notes: Solberg 3% MIL-SPEC SFFF first on DoD QPL (MIL-PRF-32725); NRL glycosiloxane surfactants matched AFFF on small jet-fuel pan fires

lab.synth: 1-2 step custom (e.g. hydrosilylation siloxane-glycoside), 3 variants x 50-100 g for foam batches
lab.test: surface/interfacial tension + spreading on heptane (ASTM D1331), expansion/drainage and small pan fire per EN 1568-3 / MIL-PRF-32725 at a fire lab (e.g. SwRI, Jensen Hughes)
lab.logic: synth 6 wk + foam formulation and fire tests 6 wk; synth $18k + fire test days ~$30k (est.)

sale.gates: foam maker formulation 1 yr; EN 1568 / UL 162 / FM 5130 certs 6-12 mo; MIL-PRF-32725 QPL 1-2 yrs; TSCA PMN
